questions.ask: What is your year of birth?
What is the five-character customer code from your welcome letter?
What is your full date of birth?

intents.hardship: Financial hardship, e.g. job loss or illness.
intents.dispute: "This is not my debt" or "I never had this card".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan or lower repayments.
intents.vague: A vague period instead of a day, e.g. "after payday".
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

assumptions: Workdays are Monday to Saturday (Saturday is a full business day). Holidays are 2026-11-21, 2026-12-08 and 2026-12-25.
The brief does not define 'next <weekday>', so the default following_week is used.

Callback days are today or either of the next two business days (within_business_days:2). The window is 09:00-18:00 Monday to Friday and 09:00-13:00 on Saturday, with no callbacks on Sunday. business_days_only is true, so holidays are excluded.
Callback max_asks is 2: if the offered times are outside the window, the agent proposes one valid time. If that is refused, the call closes as no_callback.

Identity questions are asked in this order: birth_year, customer_code, birth_date. The year is sent as 4 digits, the code as 5 capital letters or digits with no spaces, and the date as %d.%m.%Y (DD.MM.YYYY). A date said only as numbers is read day-month-year.
max_wrong is 2: one wrong answer is forgiven across the whole check and the second ends it. This matches the API summary.

The verify response has the fields ok, correct, wrong_answers (count so far), locked and identity_passed. It has no remaining-count field and no hint field, so 'left' and 'hint' are empty and the engine counts wrong answers against max_wrong. hints is empty.
Per the API, a badly formatted answer returns ok=false and does not count as a wrong answer.
get_account returns a single object 'account' (not an array), with product_id and product_kind (card or overdraft).
Amounts are in euro cents in both get_account and create_promise, so amount_scale is 100 and promise_scale is null.

Floor: for a card it is statement_minimum_cents (floor_field). The overdraft has no floor field, so floor_pct 20 with floor_round up_unit applies to it; a result that is already a whole euro is not raised. credit_limit_cents and overdraft_limit_cents are never used.

Band deadlines: early is the last business day of next week (end_of_next_week). Middle is the 8th business day after today for a card and the 5th for an overdraft. Late is the later of the last business day of the month and the 3rd business day after today.

Recoveries band (61 days or more): the validator only accepts a non-transfer event key for bands_outside, so these accounts go to a custom event 'recoveries' that closes handed_over / recoveries with no proposal, no promise and no note. Rule 32 does not list rule 22 among the rules that get a note. no_band_line says a colleague now handles the account. The spec format cannot express a transfer from bands_outside, so the transfer_to_agent call with queue 'recoveries' that rule 22 requires may not be made by the engine.

Ladder: attempt 1 is the full amount on the 2nd business day after today, or the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much. Attempt 2 (middle and late bands only) is the floor on the deadline. The early band has 1 attempt.
too_much_floor is asked_date: rule 17 offers the floor once when the full amount is too much, and per rule 20 only flat refusals or non-answers use an attempt.
deadline_adjust is previous_business_day per rule 13. If that day is before today, the first business day after the named day is offered.
Refusing the deadline after naming a date past it is a flat refusal (rule 14).
add_note is used only for paid_claim, disputed, vulnerable and system_fault. Refusals get no note.
The add_note API has no product id field. The required n_product slot is mapped to the optional free-text field 'text', so the note carries the product id as text. reason maps to n_reason.

Hardship (rule 28): add_note vulnerable, then transfer to care, then close handed_over / vulnerable. Both the hardship and transfer_support events carry note 'vulnerable' and queue 'care', so the note is written before the transfer whichever path the engine takes (rule 32). The hardship line states the transfer rather than offering it.
The brief has no rule for changing a recorded promise, so the agent says it can't be changed on this call.
The brief says nothing about the turn after a promise, so the default ask_anything_else true is kept. There is only one product, so the multi defaults are kept.

The opening states the call is recorded as 'we record this call'. The brief's exact words are used for the confirm question, 'Could you pay the full amount today?', 'Is that correct?', 'A confirmation letter will follow by post.' and 'Please accept our condolences.'
Call variables full_name and salutation are declared. The confirm question uses {full_name}, as the brief prescribes.
Every tool's success flag is ok == true.
